headline: High: shared writable workspace and overlapping file-based skill context create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; A’s no-egress limits some blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A has no shared channel documented, but agent B explicitly reads and builds on shared skill/context files, including writable filesystem surfaces. If A’s outputs are placed into those files or a shared workspace, B can ingest attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible from docs, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into any file under agent_b.io_surfaces.files, THEN B may treat them as instructions.
IF both agents share a writable workspace, THEN prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories.
Disable automatic ingestion of file contents by B.
Require provenance tags on any shared file.
Use read-only mounts for A’s outputs.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before B reads shared context.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can read files and call external APIs, while agent A’s docs show no egress and no data classes touched. If A processes sensitive material and writes it into B’s workspace, B can upload or expose it through its allowlisted network paths. The leakage path is plausible, but the sensitive data source is not documented for A, so severity stays medium.
conditions: IF agent_a is given sensitive inputs and writes them to a shared file, THEN B can read them.
IF B’s API calls include file-derived context, THEN those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive A outputs in B-readable paths.
Restrict B API calls to non-sensitive prompts.
Use separate OAuth/API credentials per agent.
Rotate or redact shared files before B reads them.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on B egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B has write_filesystem, read_filesystem, and spawn_subprocesses, plus multiple-instance support; agent A’s profile does not show write surfaces, but the pair still conflicts if both are pointed at the same directory or shared skill files. Because B’s defaults include mutable filesystem access and concurrency, collisions can corrupt shared state or overwrite A-produced artifacts. Uncertainty about A’s write surface does not reduce the risk enough to lower severity.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory, THEN file overwrites or corruption can occur.
IF B runs multiple instances against shared files, THEN race conditions become likely.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize B instances with a lock file.
Make A outputs read-only before B accesses them.
Avoid shared git state between agents.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and namespace isolation.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s sandboxing says skills reference each other and build on shared context, so B may treat upstream outputs as authoritative. A is an audio-speech/LLM-hub style repo with no verified runtime safeguards, so if its generated content is fed into B without verification, errors can cascade into downstream marketing artifacts. The interaction is inferred from docs, not reproduced.
conditions: IF A-generated text is used as B’s source context, THEN B may propagate A’s mistakes.
IF B skips independent verification, THEN downstream outputs can inherit false claims.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add a verification checklist for B.
Keep source citations alongside shared context.
Limit B to drafting, not final publication.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. A has no data classes touched and no egress, while B touches marketing content and uses allowlisted network access. Without evidence of regulated data or conflicting policies, only a low compliance concern remains, and A is not cited for a specific violation because none is shown.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into B’s marketing workflow, THEN policy review is required.
IF A is repurposed to handle residency-restricted data, THEN compliance scope changes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention for B’s marketing files.
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment.
Separate regional datasets from shared context.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and retention controls.
